title: Make one result easy to hear
objective: Use a pause, a clear voice and a simple gesture to explain a result.

slides.title: Help your audience follow a number
body: Face your listeners. Say a short phrase, pause, then give the second number.
Point to the label as you name it. Leave enough time for the audience to look.

slides.title: Try two readings
body: Say “We saw six frogs at dusk and two in the morning” quickly.
Now say “We saw six frogs at dusk / and two in the morning.”
Ask your partner which reading made the comparison easier to hear.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Slide: “Pond birds. Morning: 12. Afternoon: 5.” The slide is for first-year students.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Write one short sentence to say aloud. Add a slash where you will pause.
Say your sentence at a steady pace. Point to each number as you say it.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Slide: “Garden bees. Morning: 6. Afternoon: 14.” The slide is for first-year students.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Write one short sentence to say aloud. Add a slash where you will pause.
Say your sentence at a steady pace. Point to each number as you say it.
Ask a partner to repeat the main message. Write one change you will make.

slides.title: Use listener feedback
body: Have your partner repeat both values. Adjust one pause, gesture or stressed word, then deliver the line again.
